brief: Audience first, product second. The new founder playbook. Why distribution is the moat in 2026 and how AI lets one person own a niche.

slots.subtitle: Why the best founders own the audience before they ever ship a single line of code.
slots.preview1: How I built a 12K list before launch
slots.preview2: Why AI makes one-person niches unstoppable
slots.preview3: The burn-rate myth first-time founders believe

slots.title: Own the
slots.subtitle: Distribution is the only defensible asset a solo founder can build in 2026.
slots.insight1Title: Pick a niche you can serve daily
slots.insight1Body: Post one specific insight every day for ninety days straight.
slots.insight2Title: Give away your best thinking free
slots.insight2Body: Trust compounds faster than code when you teach without a paywall.
slots.insight3Title: Sell only after demand is obvious
slots.insight3Body: Build the product your DMs are already begging you to release.
slots.pullQuote: If nobody is asking for it, you don't have a product problem—you have a distribution problem.

slots.title: Ship later
slots.subtitle: How I validated a SaaS idea with a Google Doc and a tweet thread.
slots.insight1Title: Tweet the pain point loudly first
slots.insight1Body: My thread on invoicing headaches reached forty thousand founders in one weekend.
slots.insight2Body: I linked a waitlist, not a landing page, and collected two thousand addresses.
slots.insight3Title: Build only what they asked for
slots.insight3Body: The beta had three features because that is all the early users needed.
slots.pullQuote: Revenue is the only metric that matters before you write a single test.

slots.title: One founder
slots.subtitle: AI collapses the cost of creation so founders can focus entirely on distribution.
slots.insight1Body: I use three custom agents to draft, edit, and schedule every daily post.
slots.insight2Body: Analytics lie; replies and DMs tell you exactly what your audience will pay for.
slots.insight3Title: Move faster than teams of ten
slots.insight3Body: Speed is your moat when competitors need meetings and you ship in hours.
slots.pullQuote: In 2026, the solo operator with distribution beats the funded team without it.

slots.title: Product is
slots.subtitle: Code is cheap and trust is expensive, so stop building your product in total silence.
slots.insight1Title: Start with a service not code
slots.insight1Body: Consulting taught me exactly where customers bleed money before I automated anything.
slots.insight2Body: If you do it twice, write a script. If you do it ten times, ship.
slots.insight3Body: My changelog is public, and the top-voted feature always ships within two weeks.
slots.pullQuote: The best product in an empty room still makes no sound.

slots.title: Own your
slots.subtitle: A superior product with no audience dies quietly because distribution is the only true monopoly.
slots.insight1Title: Pick one channel and dominate it
slots.insight1Body: I chose Twitter and ignored everything else until I crossed fifty thousand followers.
slots.insight2Body: One long essay becomes a thread, a newsletter, a video script, and a podcast.
slots.insight3Title: Own the relationship not the platform
slots.insight3Body: Social accounts get banned; email lists and communities are assets you actually control.
slots.pullQuote: You do not own your audience until you can reach them without an algorithm.

slots.title: 2026 belongs
slots.subtitle: The barrier to entry is gone, and the barrier to attention is now everything.
slots.insight1Body: If your total addressable market is not tiny, you are not niche enough yet.
slots.insight2Body: Combine domain expertise with AI speed and an audience no competitor can buy.
slots.insight3Body: Profitability is a choice when your team is one laptop and a Wi-Fi signal.
slots.pullQuote: The next unicorn is a solo founder with a laptop and a loyal niche.

slots.ctaBody: Distribution beats product when nobody knows you exist. Start with the audience.
